- <a id="st-ethiopia-tigray" class="st-a"></a>**Fighting between Ethiopia's federal army and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) escalated on Thursday 24 September, with the military claiming it had killed 272 rebels, raising fears of a return to full-scale war in the country's north.** The clashes first broke out on Wednesday 23 September in the Tigray region and quickly widened; the TPLF's vice-president told AFP "we are in the situation of full-blown war now," while Ethiopia's military said its counter-offensive had inflicted "heavy personnel and equipment losses" — a claimed 272 killed and about 260 wounded that could not be independently verified and gave no breakdown of fighters versus civilians. The renewed combat threatens the fragile 2022 Pretoria peace deal that ended a two-year war in which hundreds of thousands died. The African Union and the United Nations have called for restraint and de-escalation. Why it matters: a collapse of the Pretoria agreement risks reopening one of the deadliest conflicts of the past decade and could destabilise the wider Horn of Africa. [DW, 24.09.2026](https://www.dw.com/en/ethiopia-s-military-says-it-killed-hundreds-of-tplf-rebels/a-79419173)
